text:
josh-devex: Heads-up — the eval harness CLI validator is too permissive and it's masking config errors. Local `ri-eval run local` returns exit 0 even when the runner later crashes in CI. Repro and minimal example below.

maya-research: Ugh, I ran into the exact same thing with a quantized model onboarding yesterday. Spent an hour debugging before noticing the YAML schema mismatch.

josh-devex: Repro steps:
1) Create `test_eval.yaml` with the wrong `metrics` format.
2) `ri-eval run local --config test_eval.yaml` -> completes OK (no nonzero exit)
3) CI job `eval-runner/test` fails on startup with KeyError on `metric_name`.

Example bad config: 
```yaml
eval_name: sanity-check
model: ../models/gptq-v1
runner:
  type: local
  device: cpu
metrics:
  - accuracy
  - f1
```
(validator expects `metrics` to be a mapping with thresholds or args, not a list)

sara-ml: That list vs mapping thing is subtle because older examples used a list. We changed the runtime schema when adding threshold-based alerts and forgot to update the CLI help/docs.

ben-eng: Also saw cases where `runner` was missing entirely and local harness faked a dry-run path. We should make the validator fail hard unless `runner.type` is present and supported.

josh-devex: Agreed. Proposed fixes:
- Update CLI validator to use the canonical JSON schema and enforce `metrics` type + `runner` required fields.
- Add `--strict` flag that turns warnings into errors for local runs (opt-in for now).
- Add a small unit test + an integration test that runs `ri-eval run local` on malformed configs and asserts nonzero exit.
- Update docs/examples to show the mapping form for `metrics`.

infra-bot: CI failed: job `eval-runner/test` 1758002340 -> `Traceback KeyError: 'metric_name'` in `eval_runner/core.py:312`

maya-research: For onboarding new models (especially quantized), it's painful because the harness will silently skip metric hooks if the metrics field is wrong. That produced false positives for model regression checks. We need regression alerts to be reliable.

josh-devex: I'm going to open a PR with the validator changes + tests. Drafting now: PR #4128. Will include a migration note for existing configs.

sara-ml: Please include a changelog snippet and a small migration script that can auto-convert list->mapping for simple cases (e.g., convert `metrics: [accuracy]` -> `metrics: {accuracy: {threshold: null}}`). Should reduce customer friction.

ben-eng: Also add an explicit exit code when validator fails so CI can short-circuit earlier. Right now the downstream runner raises, which hides the real root cause.

teri-sre: @josh-devex once PR is up can you notify SRE? We'll add a short alert rule to detect this class of CI failures (missing schema fields) and route to devex oncall.

josh-devex: Will do. Plan for PR: validator + --strict flag + unit tests + migration helper + small docs update. Assigning reviewers: @sara-ml, @ben-eng.

maya-research: Thanks. If you want I can add one failing eval case with a quantized model to the integration test matrix — exercised the real failure mode before.

josh-devex: That would be great, @maya-research. I'll add you to the PR.

sara-ml: :thumbsup: Let's aim to land this before the next weekly release so Dedicated customers don't hit surprises.

ben-eng: Ping me if you need help wiring the CI job to fail fast (we can add a matrix job that validates config files only).

josh-devex: Thanks everyone — opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4128
